performers: Enrico Caruso, tenor; Salvatore Cottone, piano
intro: In “E lucevan le stelle”, from Act III of Tosca, Cavaradossi has an hour to live and recalls a night with Tosca. Caruso sings it here with Salvatore Cottone at the piano.

sections.label: A · Cavaradossi recalls the night with Tosca
sections.mNote: Cavaradossi recalls the stars and the garden gate.

sections.label: B · Kisses and embraces, tenor and piano
sections.mNote: The tenor sings of holding Tosca in his arms.

cues.title: Cavaradossi’s aria, Act III
cues.text: On the roof of Castel Sant’Angelo, Cavaradossi recalls another night, with stars overhead, the scent of the earth and a garden gate creaking. The aria opens “E lucevan le stelle” (“And the stars were shining”). Caruso sings it here with piano accompaniment.
cues.evidence: Illica and Giacosa, Tosca (1900), Act III, Cavaradossi’s aria; text and setting in the La Scala libretto, pp. 38–39: https://www.teatroallascala.org/static/upload/tos/tosca-libretto-accessibile.pdf . Piano credit: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:E_lucevan_le_stelle_(1902).opus . Translation ours; the opening line has the variant lucevan/lucevano.
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: Cavaradossi’s last letter, Act III
cues.text: The jailer offers Cavaradossi a priest. Cavaradossi asks to write a last message to Tosca and offers the ring from his finger as payment for its delivery, which the jailer accepts. Before he can finish writing, he begins to remember Tosca.
cues.evidence: Illica and Giacosa, Tosca (1900), Act III, scene 2, immediately before the aria; La Scala libretto, p. 38. https://www.teatroallascala.org/static/upload/tos/tosca-libretto-accessibile.pdf

cues.title: “O dolci baci”, central lines
cues.text: Cavaradossi recalls Tosca’s footsteps on the sand, her scent and her body in his arms. He then sings “O dolci baci, o languide carezze” (“O sweet kisses, O languid caresses”).
cues.evidence: Illica and Giacosa, Tosca (1900), Act III, central lines of E lucevan le stelle; La Scala libretto, pp. 38–39. https://www.teatroallascala.org/static/upload/tos/tosca-libretto-accessibile.pdf . Translation ours; commentary on the remembered scene, without word-level timing.
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: Final line of the aria
cues.text: The aria closes with Cavaradossi facing death: “E non ho amato mai tanto la vita” — “And never have I loved life so much.”
cues.evidence: Illica and Giacosa, Tosca (1900), Act III, final sentence of E lucevan le stelle; La Scala libretto, p. 39. https://www.teatroallascala.org/static/upload/tos/tosca-libretto-accessibile.pdf . Translation ours; the established closing section locates the passage.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

composer.epithet: Composer who held a theatre audience through a scene of a woman at a window, then brought back a tune it had heard before.
facts: Lucca; Milan Conservatory, 1880–83, with Bazzini and Ponchielli
Giulio Ricordi · Luigi Illica and Giuseppe Giacosa · Giuseppe Adami and Renato Simoni
Twelve operas, counting Il trittico as three; a Mass, songs and chamber music
composer.background:
Puccini began at the organ. His family had supplied Lucca with church musicians for generations, and when his father Michele died in 1864, the five-year-old Giacomo was expected to continue the trade. He studied in the town, played in its churches and completed a Mass in 1880. In 1876, however, he had heard Verdi’s Aida in Pisa, and he turned to the theatre. A scholarship helped him into the Milan Conservatory, where Antonio Bazzini and Amilcare Ponchielli taught him composition. His graduation piece of 1883, Capriccio sinfonico, contains the music that later opened La bohème.

He submitted his first opera, Le Villi, to the Sonzogno competition on the last possible day, 31 December 1883; it did not receive a mention. The librettist Ferdinando Fontana arranged a private hearing at the journalist Marco Sala’s house, with Arrigo Boito among the guests. A subscription paid for a performance at Milan’s Teatro Dal Verme the following May. Giulio Ricordi bought the opera and commissioned another. Edgar, first performed at La Scala in 1889, was a failure that Puccini spent years trying to repair.
